questions.q: Why were Sofia's first weeks in Galway difficult?
choices: She could not find her aunt's house.
She knew nobody and found the weather colder than expected.
She was not allowed to attend her course.
Her aunt asked her to move away.
questions.explanation: The message says Sofia was lonely and surprised by the cold weather.

questions.q: What has made life in Galway more pleasant for Sofia?
choices: Her aunt no longer has to work.
The town now has warmer weather.
She has joined a basketball club.
She has made friends who often cook together.
questions.explanation: Sofia now has friends and regularly prepares meals with them.

questions.q: Why does Sofia think Noah might enjoy the Sunday activity?
choices: The museum is free for everyone.
The photographer is a relative.
She remembers Noah's interest in photography.
His basketball team will perform there.
questions.explanation: She connects the exhibition invitation with Noah's love of photography.

questions.q: What is the most likely reason Sofia needs Noah's decision by Friday?
choices: She needs time to book a ticket.
She has to return to Galway immediately.
The station closes on Friday afternoon.
The photographer will change the pictures.
questions.explanation: She requests a reply by Friday evening because she needs to reserve a ticket.

questions.q: What does the exhibition focus on?
choices: Famous athletes in competition.
Scenes from historic battles.
Ordinary people doing interesting work.
The history of Galway's weather.
questions.explanation: The collection features photographs of people engaged in their everyday jobs.

questions.q: What might visitors learn at the workshop?
choices: How to take better photos using a phone.
How to repair old bicycles.
How to become professional nurses.
How to build a railway station.
questions.explanation: The free workshop teaches techniques for phone photography.

questions.q: What is special about the bicycle repairer in Sofia's favourite photo?
choices: He owns a very large shop.
He has worked in his little shop for fifty years.
He is the photographer's grandfather.
He now works only at night.
questions.explanation: The caption describes an elderly man repairing bicycles in the same shop for fifty years.

questions.q: What will Sofia and Noah do if the photography exhibition is full?
choices: Return to Galway without meeting.
Go to the basketball stadium.
Try to photograph the old station.
Visit the science museum instead.
questions.explanation: The last paragraph offers the science museum as a backup plan.

questions.q: How does Sofia show that meeting Noah matters more than a perfect schedule?
choices: She asks him to organise every detail.
She insists on the photography exhibition.
She says even an hour together would be enough.
She tells him not to discuss his basketball team.
questions.explanation: Sofia explicitly says a short meeting would still make her happy.

questions.q: Which response best fits the tone of Sofia's email?
choices: A friendly reply about availability and Noah's recent news.
A formal complaint about the exhibition tickets.
A list of the photographer's achievements.
A refusal to talk about school or sport.
questions.explanation: Sofia makes a personal invitation and also asks how her friend is doing.
